:step/content.:tutorial/content:
If we want to add (or subtract) three or more matrices, all operations should be done elementwise. For example, suppose

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Then we can calculate ${A}+{B}-{C}$ by performing the operations on each corresponding entry, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A+B-C & =\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1+(-1)-0 \\ 1+2-5 \\ -1+0-(-2)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Performing the operations on each corresponding entry, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(B-C) & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-(\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}0 & -5 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}) \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-1-0 & -1-(-5) \\ 2-1 & 0-1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1-(-1) & 0-4 \\ 2-1 & -2-(-1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & -4 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating the Sum or Difference of Three or More Matrices

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Since addition and subtraction of matrices are performed elementwise, they have the same properties as addition and subtraction of real numbers.

For example, if $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ are three $m \times n$ matrices then we can add them in any order:

$$
(A+B)+C = A+(B+C) = A+B+C
$$

Moreover, we can distribute a subtraction over matrices in parentheses:

$$
A - (B + C) = A - B - C
$$
:step/content.:tutorial/title: Properties of Matrix Addition and Subtraction

:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, we simplify the expression by distributing the subtraction over the matrices in the parentheses: 

$$
\begin{aligned}A+C-(B+A) & =A+C-B-A \\  & =\cancel{A}+C-B-\cancel{A} \\  & =C-B\end{aligned}
$$

We are left with a single subtraction. So, we subtract the corresponding entries of the two matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}C-B & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -6 & 1\end{bmatrix}-\begin{bmatrix}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}3-3 & -1-(-1) \\ 1-2 & 2-0 \\ -6-(-4) & 1-1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

:step/content.:knowledge-point/title: Calculating the Sum or Difference of Three or More Matrices Using Distributivity
